title: Tooltip randomly loses shadow
line: Panel tooltips and popups no longer occasionally show up without their shadow.
explanation: libplasma recreates a popup's shadow (unset, then org_kde_kwin_shadow_manager.create, attach the tiles, org_kde_kwin_shadow.commit) on every show, move and resize of the tooltip, on the GUI thread. KWin attaches the new shadow object to the surface's pending state as soon as it is created, while Qt's render thread commits the wl_surface independently; a WAYLAND_DEBUG trace on the rig caught that commit landing between create and shadow.commit 2 times in 196. KWin then reads the shadow before its tiles are committed, gets an empty shadow, and never looks at it again, so the tooltip stays shadowless until the next recreation. Now a shadow.commit on the surface's current shadow marks the shadow as changed in the surface's pending state, so the next wl_surface commit re-reads the tiles.

commits.message:
wayland: Re-read a surface's shadow when its contents are committed

The shadow is set on the surface at creation time, so a wl_surface commit
arriving before org_kde_kwin_shadow.commit applies an empty shadow that is
never re-read. Mark the shadow as changed so the next commit picks it up.

BUG: 516030

media.caption: Pure master, brightness tooltip with the race forced (wl_surface.commit injected right after shadow create): no shadow around it
Same tooltip, same forced race, patched KWin: the shadow is there
Pure master, forced race: the 'Show hidden icons' tooltip has no shadow
Patched KWin, forced race: the same tooltip has its shadow
Sweep tester's natural repro on master (no shim, hovering the tray): Clipboard tooltip without shadow (top) and with it (bottom)
Patched KWin without the shim: the calendar popup and the panel keep their shadows

review.text: Impressive root-cause diagnosis and clean compositor-side fix in KWin's ShadowInterface: because org_kde_kwin_shadow_manager_create immediately set the empty shadow on the surface's pending state, a render-thread wl_surface.commit arriving before org_kde_kwin_shadow.commit applied an empty shadow that was never re-read. Marking the shadow dirty on the surface when org_kde_kwin_shadow.commit runs for the surface's current shadow cleanly resolves both the race and in-place shadow updates without clobbering pending unsets or newer shadows. Verified with a deterministic race reproducer, natural repro comparison, and passing KWin/KWayland shadow and surface autotests.

reviews.text: Impressive root-cause diagnosis and clean compositor-side fix in KWin's ShadowInterface: because org_kde_kwin_shadow_manager_create immediately set the empty shadow on the surface's pending state, a render-thread wl_surface.commit arriving before org_kde_kwin_shadow.commit applied an empty shadow that was never re-read. Marking the shadow dirty on the surface when org_kde_kwin_shadow.commit runs for the surface's current shadow cleanly resolves both the race and in-place shadow updates without clobbering pending unsets or newer shadows. Verified with a deterministic race reproducer, natural repro comparison, and passing KWin/KWayland shadow and surface autotests.

The diagnosis is concrete and checked against the code: shadow_manager.create puts the new ShadowInterface into the surface's pending state immediately, KWindowShadow only sends shadow.commit after attaching tiles, and a render-thread wl_surface.commit landing in between makes KWin build an empty shadow that is never re-read (caught 2/196 in a WAYLAND_DEBUG trace). Re-marking the shadow field on shadow.commit when it is already the surface's current shadow is a small, server-side fix in the right place, and KWindowShadow's requestUpdate() after shadow.commit guarantees the follow-up surface commit that picks it up; the pending-already-set and dead-surface cases are guarded. The forced-race shim pairs clearly show shadowless tooltips on master and shadows with the patch, plus a natural master repro and autotests. The one-frame flicker from c10 is libplasma recreating the shadow, a side observation rather than the reported persistent loss, so BUG: is fine.
